oil-and-gas-industry-influence-at-un-cli.title: Oil and gas industry influence at UN climate summit
oil-and-gas-industry-influence-at-un-cli.one_liner: At COP 31 in Antalya, Turkey in November 2026, the final agreement text removed the explicit call to "phase out fossil fuels" despite decades of scientific evidence that burning coal, oil, and gas is the primary driver of planetary warming. Critics argue that an unprecedented number of fossil fuel lobbyists—outnumbering delegations from many nations at the summit—influenced negotiations. The phrase "fossil fuel phase-out" was removed under pressure from petrostates and industry-backed negotiators. In place of emissions reductions, the final text elevated "Carbon Capture and Storage" (CCS) and "Carbon Dioxide Removal" (CDR) as cornerstones of global climate strategy. Industry representatives framed carbon capture as allowing net-zero targets while approving new offshore drilling and pipeline expansion, with a secondary revenue stream for the oil and gas sector through payments for storing captured carbon in derelict rigs and depleted oil deposits.

Research at Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest found that prescribed fire cut tree mortality by more than half during the 2020 Castle Fire, offering a proven management approach to restore ecological resilience in these ancient forests after nearly two centuries of fire suppression.

microplastics-generate-toxic-reactive-mo.title: Microplastics Generate Toxic Reactive Molecules; New Health Risks Identified
microplastics-generate-toxic-reactive-mo.one_liner: Scientists at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley discovered that microplastics generate reactive oxygen species (ROS)—highly reactive and potentially damaging molecules—when they interact with water. The research, published in Nature, identifies a previously unknown chemical mechanism by which microplastics may harm human health. As plastic fragments into smaller particles, the exposed surface area increases dramatically, enabling chemical interactions with water that produce these reactive molecules. Because blood and cells contain large amounts of water, microplastics entering the human body could continue generating ROS, which can damage cellular and tissue structures. The findings offer a potential explanation for health problems linked to microplastic exposure, including heart attacks, strokes, and neurological disorders, though the study does not establish causation of specific diseases in humans. The research builds on a 2024 Columbia study that detected approximately 240,000 plastic fragments per liter of bottled water—10 to 100 times higher than previous estimates.

scientists-propose-test-for-multiple-sim.title: Scientists Propose Test for Multiple Simultaneous Time Flows Using Enhanced Atomic Clocks
scientists-propose-test-for-multiple-sim.one_liner: Scientists at Kyushu University, collaborating with Stevens Institute of Technology, University of Waterloo, the National Institute of Standards and Technology, Colorado State University, and Stockholm University, have proposed a theoretical method to detect quantum superposition of times—a phenomenon where time could flow at multiple rates simultaneously. The approach, published in Physical Review Letters, leverages trapped-ion atomic clocks with enhanced sensitivity to test whether a clock can exist in quantum superposition, where its motion follows multiple possibilities at once. According to the researchers, quantum superposition of a clock's motion would be linked to its internal energy through entanglement, producing measurable changes detectable using modern techniques. The proposed method could boost sensitivity by up to 1,000 times compared to current approaches. This would test a theoretical prediction arising from the intersection of quantum mechanics and Einstein's relativity: if a clock's motion exists in superposition (following multiple paths simultaneously), and motion affects time's passage through relativity, then different rates of time could coexist in a single quantum state. This phenomenon has never been directly observed. The research builds on atomic clocks' capability to already detect minute differences in time's passage predicted by relativity between clocks separated by millimeters, suggesting they are sensitive enough to potentially reveal this quantum effect.

extensive-analysis-challenges-50-year-ol.title: Extensive Analysis Challenges 50-Year-Old Theory About Evolution Protecting Critical Genes
extensive-analysis-challenges-50-year-ol.one_liner: Researchers from the University of Bath published a study in PLOS Biology challenging a 50-year-old evolutionary theory that organisms protect their most essential genes by reducing mutation rates. Dr. Sofia Radrizzani and Professor Laurence D Hurst analyzed the largest collection of spontaneous genetic mutations assembled to date, focusing on the bacterium Escherichia coli and the single-celled fungus Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's yeast). The analysis found no evidence that essential genes experience lower mutation rates than other genes. The researchers attributed earlier findings supporting the theory to a methodological flaw: harmful mutations in essential genes may have disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them, creating a misleading appearance that these genes mutate less frequently. The theory was first proposed in 1972 and has been periodically revisited, including in a renewed debate in 2023. Dr. Radrizzani stated the claim that mutation is slower for important genes is "a triumph of hype over substance."

the-president-of-the-united-states-disma.title: The President of the United States Dismantles U.S. Scientific Research Infrastructure
the-president-of-the-united-states-disma.one_liner: The president of the United States' administration has dismantled multiple major U.S. scientific research programs. The National Science Foundation (NSF) began dismantling the Ocean Observatories Initiative (OOI), a $368 million deep-ocean observation program consisting of hundreds of instruments. Executive orders targeting diversity, equity, and inclusion programs have led to the termination of more than 1,700 research grants across National Institutes of Health (NIH) programs and elimination of millions of dollars in federal grants. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) lost an entire team monitoring maternal mortality. The Department of Education reclassified public health and nursing degrees as nonprofessional, restricting federal student loan access for health professions students. These actions have cut research capabilities, surveillance systems, and workforce development programs while raising costs and threatening national health security. As of June 18, 2026, a bipartisan measure by senators blocked dismantling of the Ocean Observatories Initiative, and the NSF announced it was abandoning its plan to end the program.

ai-models-may-not-replicate-human-brain-.title: AI Models May Not Replicate Human Brain Processes Despite Predicting Brain Activity
ai-models-may-not-replicate-human-brain-.one_liner: Researchers at York University discovered that artificial intelligence models can predict brain activity patterns but may rely on fundamentally different internal processes than the human brain uses. The study, led by Assistant Professor Kohitij Kar, challenged the assumption that AI systems work like the brain simply because they can successfully predict neural responses. The team developed a method called "reverse predictivity testing" to test whether the relationship between AI and brain activity works bidirectionally—if AI truly operated like the brain, brain activity should be able to predict what happens inside AI models as effectively as AI predicts brain activity. The research examined responses to 1,320 natural photographs and realistic synthetic images featuring 10 familiar subjects (bear, elephant, face, apple, car, dog, chair, plane, bird, zebra) against various backgrounds, plus 300 additional images showing the same subjects in different visual styles (outlines, drawings, simplified representations, artistic interpretations). The findings raise questions about the reliability of using these AI models as tools for understanding how the brain's visual system actually processes information, despite their widespread use in neuroscience research over the past decade.

new-research-proposes-reclassifying-anci.title: New Research Proposes Reclassifying Ancient Human Ancestors Within Genus Homo
new-research-proposes-reclassifying-anci.one_liner: Monash University researchers published a study in the American Journal of Biological Anthropology proposing that Australopithecus and Paranthropus—species that lived 4 to 5 million years ago and were previously classified separately—should be reclassified within the genus Homo alongside modern humans and early Homo species. Lead researcher Dr. Ian Towle argues that recent fossil discoveries and genetic analysis reveal that traits once believed to distinguish these groups from each other and from Homo are increasingly found across multiple groups, making traditional taxonomic boundaries difficult to justify. The researchers contend that Australopithecus and Paranthropus do not represent distinct evolutionary branches (clades) and that differences in behavior and ecology previously used to separate them have become increasingly hard to maintain. The study proposes expanding the genus Homo to encompass all human species and closely related fossil relatives from the past 4 to 5 million years to provide a more accurate representation of complex evolutionary relationships revealed by the growing fossil record.

ballistic-missile-strike-on-zelenskyys-h.title: Ballistic missile strike on Zelenskyy's hometown kills 2, wounds dozens

The dead included a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman; six children were among the wounded. The strikes damaged approximately 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools, and businesses. Local officials reported that Russian forces launched additional missiles after emergency workers arrived, targeting rescuers, medical personnel, and utility crews. Russia's Defense Ministry stated that a thermal power plant in Kryvyi Rih and a power substation in Rivne were hit, claiming both facilities supply electricity to Ukrainian military industry. The attack followed Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a 'painful' response to Ukraine's strikes on the Kerch Bridge linking Russian-occupied Crimea to Russia, which had occurred three times that week. The incident occurred as the president of the United States seeks diplomatic progress between Moscow and Kyiv, with the nearly five-year-old war showing little progress toward resolution.

sexual-abuse-systemic-in-russian-militar.title: Sexual Abuse Systemic in Russian Military POW Camp, WSJ Investigation Reveals
sexual-abuse-systemic-in-russian-militar.one_liner: A Wall Street Journal investigation documents systematic sexual violence by Russian forces against Ukrainian men during the war that began in 2022. The UN has gathered testimony in approximately 310 cases of alleged sexual violence by Russian forces, involving 280 men, 26 women, and four girls. Documented abuse methods include rape, gang rape, genital mutilation, electric shocks, and beatings to the genitals. A widely used torture method involves attaching old army field telephone wires to prisoners' genitals and administering electric shocks, referred to by guards as a "call to Putin." The report is based on testimony from Ukrainian prosecutors, UN investigators, and interviews with former prisoners of war. Ukrainian prosecutors told the Journal that patterns of abuse indicate the crimes were committed as a feature of Russia's military campaign rather than acts by individuals. A chief prison official in St. Petersburg told guards in charge of Ukrainian POWs that there were no restrictions against violence, including sexual abuse. All Ukrainian former POWs interviewed by the UN reported torture or ill treatment, with over 70 percent reporting involvement of sexual abuse. Specific cases documented include Serhii Boychuk, held for more than two years and subjected to rape with bottles and sticks and threats with a knife to his genitals; Oleksiy Sivak from Kherson, who had wires attached to his genitals and received electric shocks after hanging a Ukrainian flag; and Halyna Tyshchenko, 63, who was raped at gunpoint and paraded naked in below-freezing temperatures. Sivak now runs a support group for approximately 200 Ukrainian men alleging torture by Russian forces.

self-modifying-ai-models-can-edit-their-.one_liner: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign report that a 27B parameter open language model can rewrite its own weights without gradients or fresh training runs, with edits that persist in the checkpoint. The model performs a concrete loop: reads failures, proposes a weight edit, tests it, and retains only edits that pass. On held-out math problems, the model achieved +6.6 accuracy points on 490 pre-registered tasks across eight sequential self-edit sessions. On image benchmarks, the model repaired performance from 7% to ~70% after matrix noise corruption. The 27B scale was necessary—smaller models at 2B, 4B, and 9B failed or self-broke during the process. The work required only one GPU and hours of compute rather than a full training cluster. The research is documented in arXiv:2611.21885 and titled "Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights."

uk-labour-government-considers-abolishin.one_liner: The UK Labour government is considering abolishing the Environment Agency and Natural England, England's two largest environmental regulators, as part of a broader review of arm's length bodies. Louise Haigh, described as the de facto deputy prime minister, announced on Monday 23 November 2026 at the CBI conference that these organisations are under review alongside other regulators including Ofwat and the Drinking Water Inspectorate. The government's stated rationale is to increase political control over development approvals and reduce bureaucratic delays, framed as part of a "rewiring the state" initiative. Ministers argue that environmental watchdogs create obstruction through multiple veto powers and statutory consultees that delay building approvals for housing and infrastructure. The proposed review will assess each body's functions to determine what should be devolved, dissolved, or delivered by government departments directly. Environmental groups have opposed the plans, with Tony Juniper, chair of Natural England, countering that the organisation has helped accelerate building by streamlining protections for species such as bats and newts.

midwest-magnesium-recycler-eliminates-po.one_liner: Advanced Magnesium Alloys Corp., located in Anderson, Indiana, and one of the world's largest magnesium recyclers, has eliminated its sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) emissions. The company was the United States' largest emitter of SF6, the most potent greenhouse gas. In 2023, the facility used 10 metric tons of SF6 as a cover gas to prevent molten magnesium from burning during recycling operations, releasing it directly into the atmosphere. Those 2023 emissions were equivalent to the annual greenhouse gas pollution of approximately 60,000 automobiles. In 2024, the company switched to a climate-friendly alternative, reducing SF6 emissions to zero. The facility operates in a former General Motors plant with approximately 40 employees.

cop31-ends-without-overarching-climate-a.title: COP31 Ends Without Overarching Climate Agreement; UN Chief and Scientists Disappointed
cop31-ends-without-overarching-climate-a.one_liner: The COP31 climate conference concluded without securing an overarching agreement on climate action, disappointing UN leadership and the scientific community.

falklands-oil-development-plans-threaten.title: Falklands Oil Development Plans Threaten Unique Marine Ecosystem
falklands-oil-development-plans-threaten.one_liner: The Falkland Islands government has licensed the Sea Lion oil development project, a major deepwater operation located approximately 130 miles north of the islands. The project, operated by Navitas Petroleum with Rockhopper Exploration, plans to drill 23 wells in its first two phases, with oil processed and stored aboard the production vessel Aoka Mizu, designed for a capacity of up to 55,000 barrels per day. Environmental experts warn the development threatens a globally significant marine ecosystem. The waters around the Falkland Islands and the Patagonian shelf support large colonies of albatrosses, penguins, and seabirds, as well as feeding grounds for South American sea lions, southern elephant seals, and southern right whales. Researchers emphasize that once subsea infrastructure is installed, it cannot be removed. The project's location falls within the Falkland Islands' disputed exclusive economic zone, which is claimed by Argentina. The sovereignty dispute over the islands and their vast oil reserves remains unresolved between Argentina and the UK, the current governing authority.

ai-powered-phishing-engine-automates-sca.title: AI-Powered Phishing Engine Automates Scam Rewriting Across Multiple Chatbots
ai-powered-phishing-engine-automates-sca.one_liner: A new AI tool enables attackers to automatically generate and distribute phishing scams by repurposing content across six different chatbot platforms.

gemini-4-neon-and-gpt-62-astra-sol-model.title: Gemini 4 Neon and GPT-6.2-Astra-Sol models released targeting business productivity
gemini-4-neon-and-gpt-62-astra-sol-model.one_liner:
Google released Gemini 4 Neon on November 18, 2026, deployed across Google AI Studio, Gemini for Business, Google Antigravity, and the Gemini app. The model is designed to consolidate work across applications including spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio, and video, and is built for long-running agent workflows. This is Google's sixth model introduction since September 2026.

OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on November 18, 2026. GPT-6.2 Astra is positioned as the frontier model for the most demanding projects. GPT-6.2 Sol is designed for everyday work and is more efficient than its predecessor, GPT-6.1 Sol, delivering better results on demanding tasks with fewer tokens. GPT-6.2 Sol powers multistep agentic workflows and is described as writing clearly and naturally. GPT-6.2 Astra creates high-quality slides, spreadsheets, and documents for professional use.

Both model releases reflect a shift in the AI industry from task-specific models toward models designed to improve output across everyday enterprise work and productivity applications. Industry analysts note this represents intensifying competition among major AI vendors for enterprise user experience and workflow integration.

openai-chief-scientist-proposes-perplexi.title: OpenAI chief scientist proposes perplexity-based 'red line' for AI development
openai-chief-scientist-proposes-perplexi.one_liner: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki published an essay on November 22, 2026, proposing perplexity—a metric measuring how accurately a model predicts the next token—as a unified, cross-company standard for measuring AI model capability. On this basis, he proposed setting an industry-wide "red line" or development ceiling that would prevent developers from crossing an agreed capability threshold until monitoring and understanding capabilities reach clear milestones. Pachocki did not specify what value the first red line should be set at or when it would take effect. He disclosed internal OpenAI data showing GPT-3.5 at log-perplexity of approximately 0.99 and GPT-4 at approximately 0.91. He indicated that transformative capabilities in cybersecurity and mathematics emerge below 0.8 log-perplexity, with breakthroughs on open math problems occurring at around 0.76. Pachocki warned that AI could drive rapid pre-training progress as early as 2027, while alignment and monitoring progress is unlikely to keep pace. CEO Sam Altman publicly endorsed the proposal, calling it "one of the most important things OpenAI has published in some time." The proposal comes as Democrats, following U.S. midterm elections, prepare to strengthen AI regulation, while the president of the United States opposes broad restrictions.

spacex-dragon-returns-with-cancer-resear.title: SpaceX Dragon returns with cancer research and 3D-printed blood vessels
spacex-dragon-returns-with-cancer-resear.one_liner: SpaceX Dragon spacecraft completed an uncrewed return to Earth on November 21, 2026, splashing down in the Pacific Ocean near Los Angeles at 2:03 PM PST after undocking from the International Space Station on November 20 at 11:05 AM CST. The capsule carried scientific experiments including frozen tumor organoids that underwent experimental cancer treatments in microgravity, and a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct designed to study vascular aging and cardiovascular diseases. The mission also returned equipment used to study how specialized lighting affects astronauts' sleep during extended space missions. The cargo was part of NASA's 35th SpaceX commercial resupply mission. The experiments are intended to advance understanding of how microgravity affects living organisms, human cells, and biological processes, with potential applications for protecting astronauts on future long-duration missions and treating cancer and cardiovascular diseases on Earth.

acute-myeloid-leukemia-originates-50-yea.title: Acute myeloid leukemia originates 50+ years before diagnosis, study reveals
acute-myeloid-leukemia-originates-50-yea.one_liner: Researchers at the University of Cambridge and University College London discovered that acute myeloid leukemia (AML) can begin developing over 50 years before diagnosis. The study, published in Nature, analyzed blood samples from women in the UK Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening (UKCTOCS), examining 47 women who developed AML (average diagnosis age 72) and 46 women who remained cancer-free. In two-thirds of cases, the first cancer-driving genetic mutation appeared before age 20 and remained largely unnoticed for decades. The research used DNA sequencing and mathematical modeling to work backward and determine when mutations first emerged, how quickly affected cells multiplied, and how they competed with other blood cells as disease approached. Mutated cells grew in predictable patterns that accelerated as additional mutations accumulated. The findings suggest doctors may eventually identify people at risk years or decades before symptoms appear, potentially enabling prevention by slowing abnormal blood cell growth. AML is an aggressive blood cancer affecting approximately 2,700 people annually in the UK, with only about one in six patients surviving at least five years after diagnosis.

genmab-scores-three-late-stage-cancer-dr.title: Genmab Scores Three Late-Stage Cancer Drug Trial Wins
genmab-scores-three-late-stage-cancer-dr.one_liner: Danish biotech Genmab achieved clinical trial success with three cancer drugs within a single month, with each drug succeeding in pivotal trials in different cancer types. The company is now focused on obtaining regulatory approvals and commercial launches. For two of the three drugs, Genmab plans to commercialize without partnering with a larger pharmaceutical company. CEO Jan van de Winkel stated the focus is on "execution" regarding approval and launch of these medicines. The timing of these three trial wins in October 2026 prompted analysts to describe the achievement as a "hat trick."

type-2-diabetes-linked-to-53-higher-alzh.title: Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher Alzheimer's risk in major review
type-2-diabetes-linked-to-53-higher-alzh.one_liner: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies led by Curtin University found that people with type 2 diabetes face a 53% higher adjusted relative risk of developing Alzheimer's disease compared to those without type 2 diabetes. The research estimated that approximately 4.7 per 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes develop Alzheimer's disease annually. The study, titled "Incidence and risk of Alzheimer's disease in individuals with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis," was published in Alzheimer's Research & Therapy in 2026. Lead researcher Dr. Emmanuel Adewuyi from Curtin School of Population Health noted that this review differed from previous analyses by focusing specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease (rather than combining multiple diabetes types or dementia forms) and by measuring both relative risk and incidence of new cases to provide a clearer picture of Alzheimer's burden in the type 2 diabetes population.

alzheimers-research-reveals-critical-fla.title: Alzheimer's Research Reveals Critical Flaw in Brain's Cellular Waste Removal
alzheimers-research-reveals-critical-fla.one_liner: A new study uncovers dysfunction in the brain's waste-clearance mechanisms that contributes to Alzheimer's disease pathology.

archaeologists-reveal-iron-age-british-r.title: Archaeologists reveal Iron Age British ruler Verica may have been a woman
archaeologists-reveal-iron-age-british-r.one_liner: Archaeologists from Bournemouth University have presented evidence that Verica, the Iron Age ruler whose exile around AD 40 triggered Rome's invasion of Britain in AD 43, was female rather than male as traditionally assumed. Verica ruled the Atrebates tribe across Hampshire and West Sussex. After being forced from power, Verica fled to Rome and appealed to Emperor Claudius for assistance; Roman historian Cassius Dio recorded that this appeal motivated Claudius to invade Britain. Dr. Miles Russell, Director of Archaeological Fieldwork at Bournemouth University, identifies three lines of evidence for Verica's female identity: the name Verica ends in "a," consistent with female names of the era (similar to Cartimandua and Boudica); coins issued under Verica's rule bear the Latin title "rex," which Russell argues is gender-neutral and was used by both male and female rulers recognized by Rome, including Cleopatra of Egypt; and artistic impressions depict Verica in Iron Age dress with Roman-style accessories including gold jewelry and a Julio-Claudian hairstyle. Russell attributes the historical misidentification to the patriarchal bias of 19th-century classical historians.

scientists-discover-explosive-volcanic-e.title: Scientists discover explosive volcanic eruption at Mariana Trench's deepest point
scientists-discover-explosive-volcanic-e.one_liner: Researchers have identified an unprecedented explosive volcanic eruption at Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, perplexing the scientific community.

norwegian-energy-firms-targeted-via-micr.title: Norwegian energy firms targeted via Microsoft security flaw
norwegian-energy-firms-targeted-via-micr.one_liner: Norwegian cybersecurity authorities confirm that energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi were compromised through a Microsoft cloud security vulnerability exploited by hackers to steal credentials.

weekly-security-recap-vmware-java4shell-.one_liner: Weekly security briefing covering critical vulnerabilities including VMware 0-day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, Ruby2Shell, and related shell-based exploits.

sap-netweaver-and-cisco-expressway-vulne.one_liner: Threat actors are exploiting unpatched flaws in SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway to leak server information and execute root-level commands.

microsoft-entra-connect-health-flaw-expl.one_liner: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft Entra Connect Health to gain unauthorized access to customer cloud tenant data.

critical-aspnet-anti-csrf-library-flaw-a.title: Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allows Unauthenticated RCE
critical-aspnet-anti-csrf-library-flaw-a.one_liner: Researchers have disclosed an actively exploited critical vulnerability in the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library that enables unauthenticated remote code execution.

pegasus-lunar-terrain-vehicle-passes-nas.title: Pegasus lunar terrain vehicle passes NASA PDR, scheduled for 2028 moon launch
pegasus-lunar-terrain-vehicle-passes-nas.one_liner: Lunar Outpost's Pegasus Lunar Terrain Vehicle passed NASA's Preliminary Design Review (PDR) on November 23, 2026, becoming the first LTV to clear this milestone. The vehicle, derived from an earlier design called Eagle, is scheduled to launch to the Moon in 2028. Pegasus underwent human-in-the-loop testing with suited astronauts from Johnson Space Center, evaluating design, usability, comfort, soil mechanics, traction, and mobility with spring mesh tires. The company built three prototypes for these tests. Following PDR approval, Lunar Outpost plans to test a drivable version in simulated lunar environments, with and without NASA astronauts. Flight-ready delivery to NASA is planned for late 2027. The rover is expected to map lunar surface terrain at approximately 3.7 miles (6 km) per day and will be remotely operated initially before human missions. It will support up to three moonwalks per Artemis mission. NASA's LTV requirements include carrying up to 176 pounds (80 kg) of lunar material and tools and traveling up to six miles (10 km) on a single charge. The Pegasus is backed by $220 million in NASA funding and built on lessons from the Mobile Autonomous Prospecting Platform (MAPP) rover sent to the Moon in 2025. Astrolab's competing design, the Crewed Lunar Vehicle 1 (CLV-1), delivered a mockup to Axiom Space for evaluation by Artemis astronauts.

voyager-1-reaches-milestone-one-light-da.one_liner: NASA's Voyager 1 has reached a historic distance of one light-day from Earth in its ongoing interstellar journey.

ukraine-confirms-naval-drone-attacks-on-.title: Ukraine confirms naval drone attacks on Russian ships off Libya
ukraine-confirms-naval-drone-attacks-on-.one_liner: Ukraine's security service (SBU) confirmed it used seven domestically made naval drones launched from a mothership to strike two Russian vessels off the coast of Libya on Sunday, 23 November 2026. The operation, conducted 1,500 miles (2,400 km) from the frontline in Ukraine, targeted the corvette Merkury—one of Russia's newest vessels—which was sunk at the Benghazi naval base, and the dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Ukraine said Russia was using to transport weapons. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy released video footage of drones approaching and striking the Merkury, triggering large explosions. The SBU stated the operation demonstrated that Russian military assets have no safe routes even far from the Black Sea. Residents in Benghazi reported loud explosions and flames; local civil defence units extinguished the fire. The Merkury had been at the base under a cooperation agreement to refuel and resupply while escorting Russian cargo ships potentially carrying military supplies to Russia.

investigation-russians-with-criminal-rec.title: Investigation: Russians with Criminal Records Obtained Romanian Passports by Posing as Ukrainians
investigation-russians-with-criminal-rec.one_liner: An investigation by the Kyiv Independent and partner newsrooms (Public Record Romania, Cu Sens Moldova, Follow the Money Netherlands, Le Monde France, and the Investigative Center of Ján Kuciak Slovakia) published November 23, 2026, found that Russian nationals with criminal records obtained EU passports by fraudulently posing as Ukrainians and exploiting Romania's citizenship laws. Researchers reviewed court files from 55 civil cases involving disputed Romanian identity documents; more than 30 beneficiaries were Russian citizens, including individuals sanctioned by Ukraine for ties to Russia's war machine or organized crime. At least eight Russian citizens posed as Ukrainians to obtain Romanian documents during Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine, all receiving assistance from the same notary in Moldova. Romanian authorities charged at least 16 Russian citizens with using forged documents to obtain Romanian passports. A Romanian court is hearing over 800 civil cases to annul identity documents obtained with forged papers. These fraudulent schemes exploited Romania's repatriation process, allowing beneficiaries to obtain authentic Romanian birth certificates using forged citizenship certificates, which then enabled acquisition of genuine Romanian passports conferring EU citizenship and visa-free travel across Europe. Among identified Russian beneficiaries: a member of a powerful Chechen clan, the then-head of a Russian state-owned explosives manufacturer, and an individual linked to organized crime reports.

israeli-military-warns-netanyahu-that-ir.title: Israeli military warns Netanyahu that Iran attack risks multi-front war
israeli-military-warns-netanyahu-that-ir.one_liner: Israel's IDF leadership has warned the Prime Minister that an attack on Iran could trigger simultaneous conflicts across multiple fronts.

cop31-climate-conference-ends-without-fo.title: COP31 climate conference ends without fossil fuel consensus for first time since 2009
cop31-climate-conference-ends-without-fo.one_liner: COP31, held in Antalya, Turkey in November 2026, concluded without a consensus cover decision for the first time since 2009. The conference, which ran two days beyond its scheduled end date, failed to reach agreement on an overarching statement due to deep divisions over whether fossil fuels and carbon capture should be mentioned, and disagreements on climate financing levels from developed to developing nations. Countries did adopt several decisions including a program to help workers and communities transition away from fossil fuels and a plan to assess climate adaptation progress. The European Union, several Latin American countries, and Pacific Island states rejected the proposed text. A central aim was to set voluntary global goals for economic electrification and increase funding for developing countries to adapt to climate impacts. This outcome follows the 2023 Dubai agreement where delegates first agreed that a "just and orderly" transition away from fossil fuels is needed to slow global warming. The Marshall Islands climate envoy stated the country would not accept "false solutions" to compromise on the agreement.

un-climate-talks-collapse-for-first-time.title: UN climate talks collapse for first time in 17 years over fossil fuel language
un-climate-talks-collapse-for-first-time.one_liner: The UN climate conference ended without an agreement for the first time in 17 years on November 23, 2026. Negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, collapsed over language on fossil fuels. The European Union, Latin America, and Pacific island nations objected to a proposal by petrostates—led by Saudi Arabia and Russia—to omit mention of fossil fuels from the final agreement. Irish environment minister Darragh O'Brien said it was "unconscionable that we would have a climate pact that makes no reference to fossil fuels." The rejected draft also included no firm commitments from wealthy countries to fund a climate reparations fund for poorer nations established in 2022. The United States did not send an official delegation to the conference; since the president of the United States returned to office, the U.S. has moved to pull out of the UN climate treaty. Under UN climate process rules, any agreement requires consensus approval, giving every country—including major fossil fuel producers—effective veto power. Former vice president Al Gore called for reforming the process "to stop polluters from blocking progress." Climate Analytics head Bill Hare noted that countries refusing to accept the document "drew a line in the sand" by rejecting a pact with no reference to phasing out fossil fuels.

gpt-62-astra-solves-previously-unsolved-.title: GPT-6.2 Astra Solves Previously Unsolved Math Theorem and Invents Novel Proof Strategy
gpt-62-astra-solves-previously-unsolved-.one_liner: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra solved Smoktunowicz's gap theorem (a 2006 mathematical theorem), producing the first known formalized, machine-verifiable proof written in Lean programming language without human assistance. The theorem states that when a mathematical system multiplies its basic building blocks, growth is either quite slow or very fast with no middle ground. Because key foundations from the original proof were missing from the Mathlib math library, Astra independently developed a novel proof strategy using "capacity," a metric from existing research that measures the minimum number of elements added per computation step, rather than following the published mathematical proofs. The proof was 1,800 lines long. Astra completed this task on Autoform-Hard, a subset of Meta FAIR's AutoformBench containing 56 tasks that ten models in Meta's study failed to solve within budget. After initially attempting to quit at 47 minutes and eight dollars, the system rejected the attempt since unsolved submissions require at least $20 spent. After nine minutes of searching for a new strategy with no code input, Astra delivered the proof at the 94-minute mark, costing $21.58 total. Astra now leads the Autoform-Hard leaderboard with 49 solved tasks, ahead of GPT-6.2 Sol and Claude Fable 5.2, which each solved 48 tasks.

nvidia-poised-for-biggest-single-day-sto.title: Nvidia poised for biggest single-day stock gain in market history
nvidia-poised-for-biggest-single-day-sto.one_liner: Nvidia stock is on track for its largest single-day percentage gain in stock market history following Jensen Huang's reinstatement announcement.

fbi-and-usda-databases-hit-by-separate-c.title: FBI and USDA databases hit by separate cyber intrusions
fbi-and-usda-databases-hit-by-separate-c.one_liner: On November 23, 2026, separate cyber intrusions compromised core databases at both the FBI and the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The FBI is investigating an intrusion into the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a database used by local, state, and federal law enforcement to share records on fugitives, warrants, missing persons, stolen property, and criminal background checks. The scope and identity of attackers remain unknown. This marks the bureau's third security probe in 2026, following an investigation into suspicious activity on an internal surveillance and investigative records system in March and a September breach by cybercrime group ShinyHunters that compromised an FBI jobs portal and exposed personal data of approximately 38,000 staff members and applicants. In a separate incident, hackers penetrated a USDA database used to send financial payments to farmers. The USDA notified employees of the breach on Thursday. Two former USDA officials warned that while the breach appeared contained to the payment system, the compromised network could serve as a backdoor into food safety records and animal-borne disease research. Neither agency nor the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency responded to comment requests. Attackers remain unidentified. The breaches followed a week of technical outages across banking and air traffic control, though federal officials attributed those disruptions to routine system upgrades and vulnerability patching rather than cyberattacks, with no immediate indication the outages are linked to the FBI or USDA intrusions. The incidents coincided with the departure of White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross.

ransomware-attacks-surge-38-in-q3-2026-a.title: Ransomware attacks surge 38% in Q3 2026 as exploit techniques escalate
ransomware-attacks-surge-38-in-q3-2026-a.one_liner: Ransomware incidents increased 38% quarter-over-quarter in Q3 2026, according to Beazley Security's Threat Report. Vulnerability exploitation doubled to account for 28% of initial access in ransomware cases, compared to 14% in Q2 2026. Malware accounted for 19% of initial access incidents in Q3, up from 14% in Q2. Nearly 37,000 Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) were published during Q3 2026, an increase of almost 80% from the prior quarter. Attackers increasingly targeted internet-facing applications, cloud credentials, and overlooked systems. AI agents conducted largely automated intrusions involving vulnerability exploitation, lateral movement, and data theft. Attackers bypassed multi-factor authentication (MFA) through stolen sessions and device-code phishing. Beazley Security recommended prioritizing known exploited vulnerabilities, internet-facing applications, and systems providing access to credentials, cloud infrastructure, or critical business operations.

critical-screenconnect-flaw-exploited-to.title: Critical ScreenConnect Flaw Exploited to Hijack MSP Technician Systems
critical-screenconnect-flaw-exploited-to.one_liner: Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9), a critical vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect, to compromise managed service provider (MSP) technician workstations. The flaw allows a guest to transfer and execute malicious payloads on a connecting technician's host. Between October 20 and November 16, 2026, Huntress researchers observed at least 688,000 guest "run file" requests targeting 42 ScreenConnect servers from 29 IP addresses, with attackers spraying servers blindly using filenames like update.bat or update_<8 hex>.bat. In one documented case on November 12, 2026, a technician's workstation was exploited to run a guest-pushed batch file (update_224ac089.bat) that decoded a Telegram bot token, downloaded a malicious MSI installer masquerading as "WindowsUpdate.msi" from masterdarky[.]com, and launched a rogue ScreenConnect client pointing to an attacker relay—all within approximately 9 seconds. The batch script registered the infection with a Telegram bot. Attackers also used canary files (marker.txt) to test payload delivery and targeted attacks where batch scripts were dropped into the Windows Startup folder. The attackers obtained publicly downloadable ScreenConnect Access installers to extract relay addresses, registered unauthorized guest clients with victim servers, and created fake sessions with cryptocurrency exchange-themed names (BITMEX-BOT, KUCOIN-SRV, LAPTOP-BINANCE) to trick technicians into connecting. This activity is distinct from a separate attack wave involving SCKit malware deployment through authentication flaws in third-party ScreenConnect extensions.

crowdstrike-to-acquire-zscaler-for-439-b.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion in major security consolidation
crowdstrike-to-acquire-zscaler-for-439-b.one_liner: CrowdStrike announced the acquisition of Zscaler for $43.9 billion, creating a combined entity with over $10 billion in annual recurring revenue.

president-of-the-united-states-endorses-.title: President of the United States endorses Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia leadership
president-of-the-united-states-endorses-.one_liner: The president of the United States endorsed Nvidia's decision to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as CEO and president on November 23, 2026. In a statement on Truth Social, the president stated that "the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security" and claimed that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche had found no evidence that Huang engaged in unlawful conduct. The president emphasized that Nvidia's reinstatement of Huang was necessary for the company's success and the American economy. Huang had been under scrutiny following allegations of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a woman allegedly connected to Chinese intelligence (Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which purchased billions in Nvidia chips). This relationship had raised national security concerns about potential compromise of sensitive information or facilitation of China's access to restricted U.S. AI chips. The Nvidia board's reinstatement decision cited consultations with senior U.S. government levels. The president stated he believed the relationship with the alleged Chinese spy did not threaten national security and emphasized that no one had proven she was actually a spy. The president also called on Nvidia to continue its internal investigation of the company's compliance with U.S. export controls.

russian-missiles-enter-polish-airspace-n.title: Russian missiles enter Polish airspace, NATO chief vows defense
russian-missiles-enter-polish-airspace-n.one_liner: On November 20, 2026, Russian missiles violated Polish airspace during a large-scale attack on Ukraine. Polish authorities announced on November 22 that debris from Kh-101 cruise missiles was recovered from three sites in eastern Poland: Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik, and Mołodycz. Initial findings indicated all missiles were manufactured in recent weeks at a manufacturing plant in the Russian city of Dubna. Investigations at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik were completed; the Mołodycz investigation was scheduled to finish on November 23. During the incursion, a Swedish Air Force pilot flying a JAS 39 Gripen fighter jet under NATO command was authorized to shoot down a suspected Russian cruise missile over Poland but did not fire due to severe weather preventing target identification. The incident coincided with military exercises in Poland involving British and French troops from the so-called Coalition of the Willing. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned Russia's attacks and stressed the alliance would continue supporting Ukraine. Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz described it as one of the largest attacks since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began. Moldova and Finland also reported separate airspace violations by Russia on November 21.

anthropic-researcher-announces-ai-assist.title: Anthropic researcher announces AI-assisted proof of Riemann hypothesis
anthropic-researcher-announces-ai-assist.one_liner: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced on November 20, 2026, that he has discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis using Anthropic's Claude AI. The Riemann hypothesis, first proposed in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, is one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems and is worth a $1 million Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize. The hypothesis proposes that prime numbers follow a specific pattern along the number line. Alpöge's Claude-assisted proof runs to more than 250,000 pages and has been formalized in Lean, a computer programming language used to mechanically verify proofs. The Lean code verification is over 17 million lines long. The proof was subsequently verified by independent researchers. Alpöge stated he also believes the proof confirms the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, a broader expansion of Riemann's conjecture. The announcement caps a year during which AI systems from OpenAI and Anthropic made breakthroughs on numerous open mathematical problems, including OpenAI's solutions to the Navier-Stokes problem and over 700 papers claiming solutions to 372 open problems. This announcement came one day after Anthropic's stock market debut.

jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-fo.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO following brief resignation
jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-fo.one_liner: Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on November 23, 2026, eleven days after his resignation on November 12, 2026. Huang had resigned amid allegations of personal misconduct, specifically affairs with Nvidia subordinates. The Nvidia board unanimously voted to reinstate him. Board chair Harvey Jones remained in his newly created position following the reinstatement. The board's decision cited input from senior levels of the United States government, with the White House confirming that the president of the United States personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting hours before the reinstatement to argue for Huang's return, citing national security concerns. The board stated in its announcement that it was 'confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk' and believed 'Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia.' Nvidia's stock had tumbled following Huang's ouster, with tech stocks broadly declining. Huang stated upon reinstatement: 'I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.'

ancient-quasar-pair-from-cosmic-dawn-def.title: Ancient quasar pair from cosmic dawn defies galaxy formation models
ancient-quasar-pair-from-cosmic-dawn-def.one_liner: Astronomers discovered Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua (officially J1602+4228AB), the oldest known compact pair of quasars, existing 900 million years after the Big Bang. The two black holes powering the quasars have masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses respectively. The pair holds the record for the closest separation between two known quasars from cosmic dawn. Their rapid growth to such massive sizes in the early universe contradicts current galaxy formation models, which cannot explain how black holes became so large so quickly. The discovery combined observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Gemini North telescope on Maunakea, Hawaii. Research was led by Silvia Onorato, a postdoctoral research associate at NSF NOIRLab, and published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters. Paired quasars are theoretically expected to be relatively common due to frequent galaxy encounters and mergers, but finding and studying them is exceptionally difficult, making this close pair from such an early cosmic epoch particularly remarkable.

critical-binary-parser-vulnerability-ena.title: Critical binary-parser vulnerability enables JavaScript code injection
critical-binary-parser-vulnerability-ena.one_liner: A critical code injection vulnerability has been disclosed in the binary-parser library, tracked as CVE-2026-134814 with a CVSS score of 9.2 (also referenced as 8.1). The flaw affects binary-parser versions prior to 2.3.1 and allows attackers who control parser definitions to execute arbitrary JavaScript code in the Node.js process. The vulnerability stems from insufficient validation of user-controlled string options (length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, and values passed to namely()) that are inserted directly into generated JavaScript code without proper sanitization. According to maintainer Keichi Takahashi, the affected options are now validated as identifier paths (e.g., foo, $parent.len), with expressions like 'len - 1' rejected in favor of functions. This is an incomplete fix for the earlier CVE-2026-1245 (CVSS 6.5), a similar code injection vulnerability disclosed in January 2026. Parsing untrusted binary data with a trusted parser definition is not affected. An advisory was released by the project maintainer on November 11, 2026. Users are advised to update to version 2.3.1 or later.

router-failure-causes-worst-us-aviation-.title: Router failure causes worst U.S. aviation ground stop since 9/11

war-disrupts-global-food-system-reliance.one_liner: The Iran war has shuttered Persian Gulf refineries, disrupting sulfur production and threatening global food supplies. Sulfur, a byproduct of oil and natural gas refining, is the feedstock for sulfuric acid, which is essential for processing phosphate rock into phosphate fertilizer. The conflict has reduced phosphate fertilizer supplies by 40 percent and raised prices beyond the reach of many farmers. Over 95 percent of the world's sulfur now comes from oil and natural gas refineries; nearly half of internationally traded sulfur previously came from Persian Gulf refineries before supplies were cut off in 2026. This dependency traces to acid rain prevention efforts over 30 years ago that required refineries to strip sulfur from their products, making waste sulfur the go-to feedstock after almost all traditional sulfur mines shut down. Analysts expect the crisis will cut crop yields in 2027 and beyond, raising food prices globally for years. The World Food Programme warns that combined with El Niño, the shortage could bring hunger to at least an additional 49 million people. As the world phases out fossil fuels, the loss of waste sulfur from refineries poses a broader threat to fertilizer production and demand for sulfur in battery manufacturing and metal ore refining.

cop31-collapse-exposes-inaction-as-deadl.title: COP31 collapse exposes inaction as deadly floods and fires signal climate catastrophe
cop31-collapse-exposes-inaction-as-deadl.one_liner: Despite a year of catastrophic climate disasters, the COP31 summit's failure reveals humanity is walking knowingly into climate disaster while fossil fuel producers block progress.

president-of-the-united-states-declares-.title: President of the United States Declares 'Extreme Climate Science' Outdated
president-of-the-united-states-declares-.one_liner: The president of the United States claimed that 'extreme climate science' is 'gone' as the UN climate panel refrains from comment.

extreme-wildfire-spread-accelerates-fore.title: Extreme Wildfire Spread Accelerates Forest Ecosystem Change in North America
extreme-wildfire-spread-accelerates-fore.one_liner: A study published in Science Advances examined nearly 3,500 wildfires across western North American conifer forests between 2012 and 2023, analyzing more than 33,000 daily wildfire spread events. The research, led by Jonathan Coop at Western Colorado University and including Camille Stevens-Rumann of Colorado State University, found that fast-moving wildfires burn not only larger areas but also more severely. As fire spread rates increase, the amount of forest experiencing near-total tree mortality rises, along with the distance to surviving trees capable of reseeding burned areas. This leaves fewer surviving trees to naturally repopulate burned landscapes. The findings suggest that forests may increasingly be pushed toward long-term ecological change rather than recovery, potentially transitioning to shrublands, grasslands, or other vegetation better suited to warmer, drier conditions rather than recovering as forests. Climate change is intensifying these conditions: vapor pressure deficit (VPD) across the western U.S. between 1979 and 2020 increased primarily due to human-caused global warming, with the region passing a critical threshold around 2000. A 2016 study found that human-caused climate change caused over half of documented increases in fuel aridity since the 1970s and doubled cumulative forest fire area since 1984. In Canada, 2023 was the worst wildfire season on record, with approximately 15 million hectares burned—more than seven times the average of the preceding 10 years. The 2024 Smokehouse Creek Fire in Texas burned over one million acres, and the 2021 Dixie Fire in California burned nearly one million acres.

socio-ecological-impacts-of-the-2025-los.title: Socio-ecological impacts of the 2025 Los Angeles urban fires on communities and homes
socio-ecological-impacts-of-the-2025-los.one_liner: A Nature Communications study published April 30, 2026, examined the socio-ecological impacts of the 2025 Los Angeles urban fires on two communities at neighborhood and residential parcel scales. The research used geospatial analyses and econometric modeling to explore relationships between urban morphology, socio-demographic factors, and home destruction. Key findings: socio-ecological characteristics and scale are critical to understanding urban fire dynamics; new socio-demographic populations are being affected; urban morphology metrics prove more important than vegetation cover in determining fire impact. The 2025 L.A. fires affected highly urbanized, socio-demographically diverse communities with estimated costs of $76–131 billion USD. The study notes that urban fires require transdisciplinary approaches and unique metrics distinct from traditional wildfire analysis, paralleling 19th and early 20th century urban conflagrations but representing a re-emerging phenomenon in modern highly populated urban areas.

study-shows-sodium-bicarbonate-and-carbo.title: Study Shows Sodium Bicarbonate and Carbohydrate Co-Ingestion Improves Athletic Performance in Fatigued State
study-shows-sodium-bicarbonate-and-carbo.one_liner: Research from Liverpool John Moores University, conducted in collaboration with World Athletics, found that combining sodium bicarbonate with carbohydrate in an energy gel helps endurance athletes sustain high-intensity efforts during the later stages of competition when fatigued, with only mild gastrointestinal side effects. The sodium bicarbonate acts as a buffer against metabolic acidosis induced by intense exercise.
takeaways: Study examined sodium bicarbonate + carbohydrate energy gel during 3 hours moderate-intensity exercise followed by high-intensity efforts
Sodium bicarbonate ingestion improved performance in fatigued state compared to carbohydrate alone
Blood analysis showed sodium bicarbonate helped limit acidosis through its buffering capacity
Findings suggest practical nutritional strategy for endurance athletes in both training and competition
Only mild gastrointestinal discomfort reported with the novel gel format

microsoft-outage-triggered-surge-in-phis.one_liner: A widespread Microsoft outage triggered a significant surge in phishing email attacks. Threat actors exploited the disruption and resulting user confusion to increase their phishing campaign volume during the outage period.

cannabis-use-associated-with-earlier-ons.title: Cannabis Use Associated with Earlier Onset of Psychosis, Gap Widens With Age
cannabis-use-associated-with-earlier-ons.one_liner: A meta-analysis of 149 studies found cannabis users develop psychosis an average of 2.5 years earlier than non-users, with the gap widening to over six years in adults over 30.

new-depression-subtype-circadian-depress.title: New Depression Subtype 'Circadian Depression' Resistant to Common Antidepressants
new-depression-subtype-circadian-depress.one_liner: Researchers identified a new depression subtype called 'circadian depression,' linked to disrupted body clocks, that affects roughly one in four severe depression cases and resists standard treatment.

depression-identified-as-early-warning-i.title: Depression Identified as Early Warning Indicator of Alzheimer's Disease
depression-identified-as-early-warning-i.one_liner: Scientists found that accumulating tau protein in older adults with depression—but normal cognition—predicts faster progression toward Alzheimer's disease.

ai-and-human-collaboration-solves-famous.title: AI and Human Collaboration Solves Famous Mathematical Problem
ai-and-human-collaboration-solves-famous.one_liner: Levent Alpoge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced on November 21, 2026, that he used the company's Claude AI tool to solve the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics' most famous open problems dating to 1859. The hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and underpins broader mathematical work. Alpoge stated that the collaboration with Claude generated more than 250,000 pages of mathematical material, noting that Claude "far outpaced" him near the finish line. The proposed proof requires independent verification by other mathematicians before acceptance. Martin Bridson, president of the Clay Mathematics Institute (which offers $1 million for solutions to each of seven Millennium Prize Problems), called the announcement "of historic significance" but cautioned that "the journey from today's announcement to a place of real understanding will be long and difficult." The breakthrough is part of a broader pattern where AI has increasingly solved famous mathematical problems that occupied mathematicians for decades. The MIT News article from November 20, 2026, reports on a panel discussion titled "AI and Society: The Future of Math" where leading mathematicians discussed implications of AI's rapid mathematical productivity for human understanding, employment, and the intellectual pursuit of mathematics—a period some have termed the "mathocalypse."

kiwi-birds-return-to-wellington-hills-af.title: Kiwi Birds Return to Wellington Hills After 150 Years in Māori-Led Conservation
kiwi-birds-return-to-wellington-hills-af.one_liner: More than 250 kiwi have been reintroduced to the hills surrounding Wellington, New Zealand, marking the first wild population in the region in over 150 years. The reintroduction, led by the Capital Kiwi project in partnership with Indigenous iwi (Māori nations), local communities, and private landowners, began in late 2022. Project teams deployed more than 5,300 traps across 24,000 hectares of farmland, forestry, and suburban reserves to control stoats (Mustela erminea), the primary predator threat to young kiwi. Under the project's predator management regime, chick survival rates have exceeded 90%, compared to nearly complete mortality in unmanaged areas. Including wild-hatched chicks, the local population is estimated to exceed 300 birds. The reintroduced birds are reported to be in good condition and laying eggs. The translocations followed traditional Māori protocols, including formal gifting requests (tono) and welcoming ceremonies (pōwhiri). Project founder Paul Ward and Kaimanaaki Kiwi (kiwi guardian) Rawiri Walsh emphasized that the initiative reflects Māori values of stewardship and restoration of treasured species (taonga) to the whenua (land).

cop31-negotiations-collapse-without-clim.title: COP31 Negotiations Collapse Without Climate Agreement
cop31-negotiations-collapse-without-clim.one_liner: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) collapsed on November 23, 2026, in Antalya, Türkiye, without adopting an overarching political agreement after nearly 200 nations failed to reach consensus. The impasse ended the longest UN climate summit on record after more than 49 hours of overtime negotiations, marking the first failure to formally adopt a political pact since the 2009 Copenhagen climate conference (COP15). COP31 President Murat Kurum ruled the proposed final text could not be adopted after the European Union, the United Kingdom, Norway, and Panama rejected draft language omitting any reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels. Major oil-producing states, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, opposed naming fossil fuels in the pact. Developing nations such as Kenya and Ghana criticized inadequate financial support and the removal of a proposed $120 billion adaptation finance target. The United States sent no official delegation for the second consecutive year following its withdrawal from the Paris Agreement. UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated in an official statement that while there is no consensus in the negotiating room, there is no ambiguity in the science, and every delay makes the climate task harder and more costly. Despite the collapse of the overarching political pact, parties still adopted technical decisions advancing a just transition framework, climate finance, and adaptation. Voluntary initiatives included pledges from 150 countries backing a target of 35 percent global electrification by 2035. The 2023 UAE Consensus from COP28, which calls on nations to transition away from fossil fuels, remains in effect. Parties will reconvene at COP32 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, next year to resume negotiations.

american-chestnut-trees-return-after-nea.title: American Chestnut Trees Return After Nearly a Century of Functional Extinction
american-chestnut-trees-return-after-nea.one_liner: American chestnut trees, functionally extinct in the United States for nearly a century due to a parasitic blight, are being restored through new breeding and propagation techniques. The American Chestnut Foundation (TACF) has conducted research since the late 1960s at orchards in Virginia's Lesesne state forest, where healthy specimens now thrive, including a tree over 70 feet tall nicknamed 'Thompson' and a 15-meter-tall pure American chestnut named 'Gladys.' Historically, American chestnuts comprised an estimated one in four trees in Appalachian and eastern North American forests. The species was prized for its fast-growing, rot-resistant wood; sweet nuts that provided food for humans and wildlife; and tannins for leather production. New resistant strains have been created to combat the parasitic blight that nearly eliminated the species.

sanofi-acquires-insmed-for-41-billion-in.one_liner: Sanofi is acquiring Insmed for $41 billion, described as the largest biopharma acquisition in years. quantinuum-achieves-record-low-quantum-e.title: Quantinuum achieves record-low quantum error rate of 0.0005%
quantinuum-achieves-record-low-quantum-e.one_liner: Quantinuum's Helios processor achieved a record failure rate of just 0.0005%, suggesting fault-tolerant quantum systems may require far fewer qubits than previously anticipated.

ancient-moon-rocks-rewrite-solar-system-.title: Ancient Moon Rocks Rewrite Solar System Bombardment History
ancient-moon-rocks-rewrite-solar-system-.one_liner: Scientists from Curtin University analyzed ancient rocks from the Moon's far side and found evidence challenging the decades-old theory of a single catastrophic bombardment period. Instead, the data shows asteroid impacts declined gradually over billions of years. The analysis identified impact events spanning approximately 4.33 billion to 1.13 billion years ago—a record covering more than three billion years. The Moon's far side rocks preserve a cleaner record of early impacts than the near side because they were less affected by later geological events. Dr. Fred Jourdan, a research co-author from Curtin University's School of Earth and Planetary Sciences and John de Laeter Centre, stated that lunar rocks act as a time capsule preserving Solar System history erased from Earth by erosion, plate tectonics, and other processes. The findings have implications for understanding Earth's earliest history and the conditions that influenced the origins of life.

global-warming-halted-earths-already-beg.title: Global warming halted Earth's already-begun ice age, ancient Arctic plants reveal
global-warming-halted-earths-already-beg.one_liner: Scientists at Columbia Climate School analyzed ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic and found that Earth's next ice age began approximately 2,000 years ago but was halted by global warming. The ice sheet started expanding again around that time, marking the possible onset of a new glacial period. However, by the 1960s, rising summer temperatures reversed this trend, causing the ice to retreat instead of continue growing. The research, published in Science, was conducted by geochemists Nicolás Young and Joerg Schaefer and colleagues. The Barnes Ice Cap is a surviving remnant of the Laurentide Ice Sheet, located on central Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada, covering an area roughly the size of Delaware. The findings indicate that global warming interrupted a natural climate cycle that has shaped Earth for millions of years, with Young stating the warming 'jolted the system' by stopping an ice age that was already underway.

new-quasar-discovery-breaks-distance-rec.title: New quasar discovery breaks distance record, constrains black hole formation models
new-quasar-discovery-breaks-distance-rec.one_liner: Astronomers led by Julien Wolf at the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy discovered the most distant quasar to date using ESA's Euclid space telescope. The quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed 'Dún Aonghasa' by the team, has a redshift of z = 8.13, placing it 630 million years after the Big Bang—40 million years earlier than the previous record holder and the first quasar with redshift greater than eight. Initial observations came from the Euclid Wide Survey, with confirmation provided by the W.M. Keck Observatory, Hubble Space Telescope, Large Binocular Telescope, and James Webb Space Telescope. The quasar contains a supermassive black hole that already existed at this early cosmic epoch. The discovery supports the scenario in which supermassive black holes form through direct collapse of large gas clouds and subsequently accumulate additional matter, constraining early black hole formation models.

check-point-security-servers-compromised.title: Check Point Security Servers Compromised in 22-Organization Campaign
check-point-security-servers-compromised.one_liner: A threat actor tracked as GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13) has compromised Check Point Security Management servers across at least 22 organizations in a campaign that began in early October 2026 and was likely still ongoing as of November 2026. The campaign targeted organizations in the energy, engineering, financial services, government, manufacturing, mining, and transportation sectors across the US, UK, Australia, Austria, China, France, Germany, Hong Kong, the Netherlands, South Korea, and other geographies. GT13 conducted scanning, exploitation, and control activities from 99 IP addresses, many associated with disposable network infrastructure or compromised victim Check Point devices. The threat actor used AI-enabled offensive tools and agentic harnesses to weaponize vulnerabilities, find vulnerable assets, and automatically exploit them, complemented by hands-on-keyboard activity. Attack activity was confirmed between October 17 and November 2, 2026. The actor deployed tools including Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and Python utilities to perform reconnaissance, lateral movement, and privilege escalation. GreyNoise documented over 1,400 network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1,200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created. Data was exfiltrated from 24 distinct Check Point Security Management servers using a compromised victim server as an operational relay box. In one tracked instance on October 2, the threat actor forged a signed admin session cookie to gain administrative access to an HFS server and obtained SSH access to scan the environment and exfiltrate data. GreyNoise could not determine when or how GT13 initially gained access to the Check Point assets. The campaign does not appear focused on any specific geography or industry sector. GreyNoise has not attributed GT13 to any known publicly tracked threat group and lacks sufficient information to assess actor motivation or nation-of-origin alignment.

cisa-warns-of-exploited-n-able-email-sec.title: CISA Warns of Exploited N-able Email Security Vulnerability; Agencies Have Until Thanksgiving to Patch
cisa-warns-of-exploited-n-able-email-sec.one_liner: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued a warning about an actively exploited vulnerability in N-able's critical email security platform, setting a Thanksgiving deadline for government patching.

cisa-adds-actively-exploited-n-able-mail.one_liner: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency listed two critical vulnerabilities in N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label as actively exploited in the wild.

amazon-reports-ai-agents-discovered-and-.title: Amazon Reports AI Agents Discovered and Exploited Zero-Day Vulnerability with Minimal Human Input
amazon-reports-ai-agents-discovered-and-.one_liner: Amazon reported that AI agents running on the Cairn framework discovered and exploited a zero-day vulnerability in an open source medical imaging AI application with minimal human input. Hackers provided only a simple instruction—to obtain shell access on an East Asian university server—along with a list of IP addresses and prompts in simplified Chinese, with the system configured to Chinese Standard Time zone. The agents autonomously found the previously unknown vulnerability and gained full control of the target system without further human oversight. Cairn is an open source AI penetration-testing framework designed for defenders that can be used with multiple AI models including Claude Code, Codex, and Pi, though it has also been adopted by attackers. Palo Alto Networks previously documented a separate campaign in which hackers used Cairn to conduct 25 autonomous operations against at least 19 organizations in the semiconductor, defense, and civil society sectors, resulting in at least 10 successful breaches where agents accessed credentials, exposed over 1 million personal records at one organization, retrieved military and government identities, created persistent administrator accounts, and modified industry standards documents. Amazon stated that these findings demonstrate that agentic offensive operations are already occurring and that defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable.

ukraine-sinks-russian-warship-strikes-ca.title: Ukraine Sinks Russian Warship, Strikes Cargo Vessels Across Multiple Theaters
ukraine-sinks-russian-warship-strikes-ca.one_liner: Ukrainian explosive naval drones sank the Russian missile corvette Merkury in the port of Benghazi, Libya on November 22, 2026. Ukraine's Security Service deployed seven naval drones launched from a mother ship; at least two struck the Merkury, which caught fire and sank. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy released video footage showing drone boats striking both the Merkury and the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which was being escorted by the corvette. A Ka-27 combat helicopter aboard the Merkury was also destroyed. Zelenskyy stated the MV Angara was transporting weapons. At least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were killed in the strikes; some crew members from the Merkury were wounded and transferred to local hospitals. The Merkury was a Steregushchiy-class missile corvette (Project 20380) equipped with anti-ship and air-defense missiles, torpedoes, and a naval cannon. It was originally assigned to Russia's Black Sea Fleet but could not enter the Black Sea after Turkey invoked the 1936 Montreux Convention following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine; the vessel instead operated from Russia's Northern Fleet bases in Arctic waters. The attack demonstrates Ukraine's expanding geographical reach with sea drones, striking Russian targets from the Mediterranean to the Baltic Sea region.

china-investigates-fourth-politburo-memb.title: China Investigates Fourth Politburo Member in Major Party Leadership Purge
china-investigates-fourth-politburo-memb.one_liner: Chinese authorities placed Shanghai party boss Chen Jining under corruption investigation, marking the fourth Politburo member probed since 2025 in an escalating purge.

england-records-5258-summer-heat-related.title: England Records 5,258 Summer Heat-Related Deaths in 2026, Nearly Double Previous Peak
england-records-5258-summer-heat-related.one_liner: England recorded 5,258 heat-related deaths between May and September 2026, according to the UK Health Security Agency, the highest provisional annual total since records began in 2016. This nearly doubles the previous peak of 2,985 deaths in 2022. The summer included seven heat episodes spanning 41 total days. The deadliest period was June 21-28, with an estimated 2,401 deaths. Temperatures reached 38°C in Norfolk in June and 38.2°C in Gloucestershire in August. England also experienced its driest July on record with 7mm of rain. The June heatwave triggered only the second red heat-health alert ever issued in England. Prior annual totals were 2,295 deaths in 2023, 1,311 in 2024, and 1,504 in 2025. UKHSA's principal environmental health scientist stated that climate change is already affecting people's health in England, and extreme heat periods are expected to become longer, more frequent, and more intense as the climate continues to warm.

vmware-vcenter-hit-by-critical-98-rated-.title: VMware vCenter hit by critical 9.8-rated authentication bypass flaw
vmware-vcenter-hit-by-critical-98-rated-.one_liner: Broadcom released patches for 23 vulnerabilities across VMware products (ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, and Avi Load Balancer) on November 24, 2026. The critical flaw CVE-2026-123903, rated 9.8 on the CVSS scale, is an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service (vmdir) that allows a malicious actor with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. Four additional high-severity vulnerabilities in vCenter were also patched: CVE-2026-123904 (arbitrary file write, CVSS 7.5), CVE-2026-123905 (denial-of-service, CVSS 7.5), CVE-2026-123906 (denial-of-service, CVSS 7.5), and CVE-2026-123907 (denial-of-service, CVSS 7.5). Fixed versions include vCenter 8.0 U3m, vCenter 7.0 (via Broadcom Support), Cloud Foundation 9.1.2, Cloud Foundation 9.0.2.0300, Cloud Foundation 5.2.5, and Telco Cloud Platform versions with vCenter 8.0 U3m. The vulnerability is distinct from the recently patched CVE-2026-123890 (also rated 9.8), another authentication bypass in vmdir that was exploited as a zero-day by suspected China-nexus group Armory Castle. No active exploitation of CVE-2026-123903 has been reported in the wild.

whmcs-sql-injection-vulnerability-expose.title: WHMCS SQL injection vulnerability exposes customer data and admin password hashes
whmcs-sql-injection-vulnerability-expose.one_liner: WHMCS, a billing and automation platform used by web hosting companies, disclosed three SQL injection and related vulnerabilities on November 24, 2026. The most critical flaw, CVE-2026-82981 (CVSS 8.7), requires no authentication and allows attackers to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from the database. A second SQL injection, CVE-2026-82979 (CVSS 7.1), requires a logged-in client with View & Manage Contacts permission to access other customers' personal, billing, and support information as well as admin records. A third vulnerability, CVE-2026-93700 (CVSS 9.0), in the email campaign functionality allows logged-in clients to read sensitive configuration files including database credentials and potentially execute code on the server. Fixed versions released November 24 include 9.0.10, 8.13.8, and 9.1.2. Self-hosted administrators must manually update; WHMCS Cloud installations update automatically. For the email campaign flaw, administrators must delete all campaigns and clear the template cache before updating. All three flaws were reported by a single researcher using the handle alakazamspooon. No attacks using these vulnerabilities have been reported. This marks the third round of WHMCS security fixes in 2026, following an authorization flaw in May and an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in September.
